sensors.installFlow.title: Install a sensor
sensors.installFlow.nameInvalid: Letters, digits, spaces, dots, dashes and underscores; start with a letter or digit.
sensors.installFlow.intro: A sensor runs inside your network. It scans what the platform can't reach and sends the results back over HTTPS. It only connects out, so you don't open any inbound port.
sensors.installFlow.name: Name
sensors.installFlow.roles.scanner.label: Scanner

sensors.installFlow.roles.collector.hint: Collects assets and telemetry, no scanning
sensors.installFlow.scannerNote: The sensor reports which scanners it has when it connects; jobs use every one of them.
sensors.installFlow.copyKeyBody: It is shown only once and is already in the commands below. If you lose it, an admin can rotate it, which disconnects the old key.

sensors.state.offline.label: Offline

sensors.optIns.interactsh.label: Allow out-of-band callbacks (interactsh) in sensor jobs
sensors.optIns.interactsh.help: Off: the platform sends no job that turns interactsh on and removes allow_interactsh from scans when they start. On: such jobs go only to sensors whose own local policy allows them; the callbacks reach an external server.
sensors.optIns.customTemplates.label: Allow custom templates in sensor jobs
sensors.optIns.customTemplates.help: Off: scans with custom templates are refused when they start and none are sent. On: they go only to sensors whose local policy allows custom templates and that pin your template signing key.
sensors.optIns.audited: Turning it on is audited and alerted.
sensors.httpPolicy.ua.label: User-Agent of scan tools
sensors.httpPolicy.ua.help: Sent by your scan tools instead of their own, so the owners of the scanned systems recognize your scans in their logs. A sensor whose local policy sets its own User-Agent keeps it. Empty: each tool sends its own.
sensors.httpPolicy.tls.label: Refuse tools that skip TLS certificate verification
sensors.httpPolicy.tls.help: On: a scan tool configured to skip certificate verification toward its targets is refused on every sensor. Turning it off again is audited.
sensors.facets.attentionHint: Results piling up, a key expiring, a version below the minimum
sensors.health.zonesCovered: every zone has an online sensor
sensors.list.groupBy.label: Group sensors
sensors.list.title: Organization sensors
sensors.list.description: The scanners and collectors that run inside your networks. CI/CD pipelines have their own page.
sensors.list.zoneGap: no online sensor, scans here will wait
sensors.list.noZoneHint: takes jobs that no zone claims
sensors.list.csv.name: Name
sensors.list.search.placeholder: Search name, host, IP, version or tool…
sensors.list.search.label: Search sensors
sensors.list.legend: Each sensor is judged against its own heartbeat interval. Online: its next heartbeat is not yet due · Late: past due, still takes work · Stale: well past due, takes no new work · Offline: over 3 intervals (at least 90s) past due, at most {offlineAfter} without a heartbeat · Idle (CI): a CI sensor between runs
sensors.control.title: Control channel
sensors.control.gapHint: Time between the last two heartbeats that reached the platform
sensors.control.lagHint: How late the heartbeat timer fired: the sensor waiting for a CPU
sensors.control.buildHint: How long building the heartbeat report took (tool probes, snapshot)
sensors.snippets.loadFailed: Could not load the install commands (HTTP {status})
sensors.snippets.policyNote: The owner of the network this sensor scans reviews this policy and installs it read-only on the sensor host (the install commands mount it). The sensor refuses every job outside it; the platform cannot change it. Needs a sensor release later than v0.8.0: v0.8.0 and older ignore the policy and scan without it.
sensors.snippets.caNoteBefore: This platform uses a private certificate authority. The commands install it and set
sensors.snippets.caNoteAfter: ; without it the sensor stops with "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority".
sensors.contentPolicy.err.digest: A digest: sha256: and 64 lower-case hex digits
sensors.contentPolicy.err.tag: A release tag such as v10.4.9
sensors.contentPolicy.pinHelp.digest: Pin a database by its OCI digest (sha256:…). Empty: the newest the mirror has.
sensors.contentPolicy.pinHelp.tag: Pin a template release (v10.4.9). Empty: the newest release.
sensors.contentPolicy.savedSent.one: Content policy saved and sent to {count} sensor.
sensors.contentPolicy.savedSent.other: Content policy saved and sent to {count} sensors.
sensors.contentPolicy.saved: Content policy saved. Sensors get it with their next refresh request.
sensors.contentPolicy.saveError: Could not save the content policy
sensors.contentPolicy.schedule.title: Refresh schedule
sensors.contentPolicy.schedule.descripti: How often sensors check for new content. Content older than its maximum age is refreshed at the next check, and the sensor shows as degraded until it is.
sensors.contentPolicy.content.title: Content
sensors.contentPolicy.content.descriptio: Maximum age and an optional pinned version per kind of content. Empty fields use the platform default shown in grey.
sensors.contentPolicy.rulesetsHelp: Empty: semgrep fetches its own rules on every scan (--config auto, not controlled). Rulesets here are fetched, verified and pinned by the sensor, and change the rules scans use.
sensors.contentPolicy.applyNowHint: Sends the policy with a refresh request to every sensor that manages its content.
sensors.contentPolicy.page.title: Scanner content
sensors.contentPolicy.page.description: How fresh the vulnerability databases, templates and rules your sensors scan with must be.
sensors.contentPolicy.sourceNote: Where content comes from (registries, mirrors, a local directory for air-gapped hosts) is configured on each sensor host, never here, so the platform cannot point sensors at other content.
sensors.contentPolicy.needsAdmin: Changing the content policy needs an admin.
sensors.grant.err.changed: The grant changed since you opened it. It was reloaded; review it and try again.
sensors.grantEdit.title: Edit grant
sensors.grantEdit.description: Currently {profile}. Narrowing takes effect on the sensor's next request.
sensors.grantEdit.profileKeeps: The zones stay as they are; the trust level does not change.
sensors.grantEdit.profileNote: Whether a profile narrows or widens this grant is decided by the server; widening needs the permission to widen sensor grants.
sensors.grantEdit.allowPush: May send results without a job
sensors.grantEdit.remoteAlways: Pause, resume, drain and cancel are always allowed.
sensors.grantEdit.widenAudited: Widening is audited at high severity and every administrator is notified.
sensors.grantEdit.widenRefused: You can only narrow grants; saving this will be refused. Ask someone with the permission to widen sensor grants.
sensors.identityPolicy.required: New sensors now join only by pairing
sensors.identityPolicy.allowed: Sensor API keys are allowed again
sensors.identityPolicy.error: Could not change the sensor identity policy
sensors.identityPolicy.label: Require key-bound sensor identity
sensors.identityPolicy.description: On: new sensors join only by pairing, with a key they make themselves; no sensor API key can be created. Sensors that already have an API key keep working. Turning it off needs the permission to widen sensor grants and is audited.
sensors.pair.title: Pair a sensor
sensors.pair.description: The sensor makes its own key. You compare a fingerprint; no key is copied.
sensors.pair.approvedBody: {who} finishes pairing on its own within 10 minutes and then appears in the list. It starts at trust level New: passive work only, no credentials, until an administrator promotes it.
sensors.pair.err.lookup: Could not look up the code
sensors.pair.err.create: Could not create a pairing code
sensors.pair.err.rateLimited: Too many attempts. Wait a few minutes and try again.
sensors.pair.err.stepUpFailed: Re-authentication failed. Check the code or password.
sensors.pair.err.stepUpRequired: Re-authenticate to approve: enter your authenticator code or password.
sensors.pair.err.fingerprint: Confirm that the fingerprint shown on the sensor matches before approving.
sensors.pair.err.busy: Too many open pairing requests. Try again shortly.
sensors.pair.err.forbidden: You do not have permission to do this.
sensors.pair.codeHelpBefore: Start the sensor on the host (or run
sensors.pair.codeHelpAfter: ). It prints a code and a fingerprint. Enter the code here.
sensors.pair.expectHelp: Get a single-use code (valid 10 minutes), run the command on the host, then compare the fingerprint the sensor prints with the one shown here.
sensors.pair.runOnHost: Run this on the sensor host:
sensors.pair.expired: The code expired. Get a new one.
sensors.pair.waiting: Waiting for the sensor to connect · expires in {time}
sensors.pair.repairBody: Approving replaces this sensor's key: its current keys are revoked and it returns to trust level New. Its history is kept.
sensors.pair.noHandshake: The sensor has not finished its handshake yet; the fingerprint appears when it does.
sensors.pair.factsNote: Hostname, system and version are what the sensor says about itself. The address is where the request reached the platform from; make sure it is a network you expect.
sensors.pair.name: Name
sensors.pair.profileDesc.internal-networ: Scans and validation in the chosen zones; no credentials.
sensors.pair.profileDesc.easm-external: Scans of internet-facing targets only; no private addresses, no credentials.
sensors.pair.profileDesc.authenticated-s: Like the internal scanner, and may receive scan credentials once trusted.
sensors.pair.profileDesc.collector: Runs one connector; no target scanning.
sensors.pair.profileDesc.ci-runner: Code scanning only; no network targets.
sensors.pair.profileDesc.endpoint-agent: Inspects its own host only; no network targets.
sensors.pair.fingerprintMatches: The fingerprint shown on the sensor console matches the one above
sensors.pair.stepUpHint: Approving a sensor needs you to confirm it is you.
sensors.pair.recentSignIn: You signed in recently, so no code is needed. If approval is refused, sign in again.
sensors.pair.needsPermission: Approving needs the permission to approve sensors. Ask an administrator.

sensors.optInBanner.title: Some scans ask for sensor features your organization has turned off
sensors.optInBanner.body: Out-of-band callbacks (interactsh) and custom templates are off by default. Scans that ask for interactsh run without it; scans with custom templates are refused when they start.
sensors.optInBanner.ownerBefore: An owner can turn them on in
sensors.optInBanner.ownerAfter: . Turning one on is audited and alerted, and a sensor still refuses what its own local policy does not allow.
sensors.regenerate.noKey: The new API key was not in the response
sensors.regenerate.failed: Failed to rotate the API key
sensors.regenerate.newKeyBody: The old key no longer works. Copy the new one now: it is shown only once.

sensors.regenerate.issueBefore: Issue a new API key for

sensors.regenerate.warnBody: The sensor disconnects until it is restarted with the new key.

sensors.localPolicy.desc.enforced: The network owner installed a local policy. The sensor refuses every job outside it.
sensors.localPolicy.desc.paused: The sensor owner engaged the local kill switch: the sensor runs no job until it is released.
sensors.localPolicy.desc.absentRequired: This sensor requires a local policy and has none: it refuses every job with a network target until the network owner installs one.
sensors.localPolicy.desc.absent: No local policy: the sensor runs any target outside its built-in deny list. Install one from the Install tab.
sensors.localPolicy.desc.notReported: This sensor runs an SDK that does not report a local policy.
sensors.localPolicy.guidance.1: Custom templates: refused by the sensor unless SENSOR_TEMPLATE_SIGNING_KEYS is set on the host, and sent by the platform only when your organization allows custom templates.
sensors.localPolicy.guidance.2: Out-of-band callbacks (interactsh): used only by a job that asks for them, and the platform sends such jobs only when your organization allows interactsh.
sensors.localPolicy.guidance.3: To decide on the host, install /etc/openctem/sensor-policy.yaml with allow_custom_templates and allow_interactsh (the Install tab renders one with both off).
sensors.localPolicy.title: Local policy
sensors.localPolicy.pausedTitle: Paused by the local kill switch
sensors.localPolicy.pausedBody: The owner of this sensor host stopped every job. Jobs wait on the platform until the kill switch is released on the host.
sensors.localPolicy.requiredBody: This sensor refuses every job with a network target, custom templates and callbacks until the network owner installs a policy (the Local policy tab of the install commands).
sensors.localPolicy.noneBody: This sensor accepts any target outside its built-in deny list. Install the policy from the Install tab so the network owner decides what it may scan.
sensors.localPolicy.digestHint: The digest the sensor reports for its local policy
sensors.contentCells.skipped: ({count} skipped: already queued or not supported).
sensors.contentCells.error: Could not request a content refresh
sensors.contentCells.confirmDesc.one: {count} sensor will download and verify the latest scanner content (vulnerability DB, templates, rules) allowed by your content policy. Running scans keep the content they started with.
sensors.contentCells.confirmDesc.other: {count} sensors will download and verify the latest scanner content (vulnerability DB, templates, rules) allowed by your content policy. Running scans keep the content they started with.

sensors.contentSection.requested: Refresh requested. {name} picks it up on its next poll.
sensors.contentSection.unmanaged: {name} cannot refresh its content: it does not manage any.
sensors.contentSection.unmanagedLine: Content fetched by the tool on each scan (not controlled).
sensors.contentSection.cannotRefresh: This sensor does not manage its content, so it cannot refresh it. Upgrade the sensor.
sensors.table.emptyDescription: Clear a filter or search for something else
sensors.activity.peopleHidden: Administrator actions are visible to owners and administrators
sensors.activity.emptyDescription: Restarts, upgrades, protocol and tool changes, connection changes, jobs and administrator actions will appear here as they happen.

sensors.activity.audit.key_renewal_refus: API key renewal refused (the key was revoked)
sensors.activity.audit.commands_released: Jobs it held taken back (re-queued or failed)
sensors.review.toolsHint: Jobs can use every installed tool. To narrow them, edit the sensor grant.
sensors.review.noToolsHint: That is normal for a collector or a custom sensor. There is nothing to choose.
sensors.review.toolsUnknown: It has not reported its tools.
sensors.review.toolsUnknownHint: Older sensors do not send a tool list. This updates by itself if one arrives.

sensors.setup.unknownCheck: The platform does not know this check yet (a newer sensor). Its data is shown as the sensor sent it.
sensors.setup.col.name: Name
sensors.setup.secret: secret · value never leaves the sensor
sensors.setup.derivedFallback: This sensor does not send a setup report; these checks are what the platform can tell from its heartbeat.
sensors.setup.staleBody: The sensor has not sent its current setup report, so these results may no longer be true.
sensors.setup.truncatedBody: The report was too large and the sensor cut it to fit, so some checks are missing.

sensors.setup.empty: This sensor has not sent a setup report yet. Sensors send one when they start and after a configuration change.
sensors.posture.title: Security posture
sensors.posture.note: Reported by the sensor. The platform flags a weak posture but never relaxes a check because of it.
sensors.posture.fix.policyNone: Install a local policy (the Local policy tab of the install commands).
sensors.posture.fix.pinNone: Pin the platform CA with SENSOR_CA_FINGERPRINT.
sensors.posture.fix.networkUnenforced: Tools run without network confinement: run with SENSOR_SANDBOX_NETWORK=required and the seccomp profile.
sensors.posture.fix.bearerKey: Pair the sensor again with an enrollment token for a key-bound identity.
sensors.keyBindPolicy.label: Require approval of sensor keys
sensors.keyBindPolicy.description: Off (default): a sensor with an API key replaces it with a signing key it makes itself, once and audited; its API key then stops working. On: such a sensor keeps its API key until an administrator re-pairs it. Turning it off needs the permission to widen sensor grants.
sensors.keyBindPolicy.requiredToast: Sensor keys now need an administrator to re-pair the sensor
sensors.keyBindPolicy.allowedToast: Sensors may replace their API key with their own signing key
sensors.keyBindPolicy.error: Could not change the sensor key policy

sensors.transport.label: Transport: {binding}
sensors.transport.reason.forced_by_confi: Set by the sensor's SENSOR_TRANSPORT setting.
sensors.transport.reason.not_key_bound: The sensor signs in with an API key, not its own signing key.
sensors.transport.reason.platform_withou: The platform does not serve protocol v3.
The platform offers the HTTPS binding only.
sensors.transport.reason.certificates_un: The sensor could not get its client certificate.
sensors.transport.reason.grpc_unreachabl: The sensor cannot reach the gRPC endpoint (DNS or firewall).
sensors.transport.reason.handshake_faile: TLS to the gRPC endpoint failed, often a TLS-inspecting proxy.
sensors.transport.reason.http2_refused: Something on the network path speaks only HTTP/1.1.
sensors.transport.reason.stream_reset: The gRPC connection keeps being reset on the way.
sensors.transport.reason.grpc_unimplemen: The platform's gRPC endpoint does not offer this call.
sensors.transport.reason.grpc_failed: The gRPC binding failed; the sensor tries it again later.
sensors.transport.reason.https_binding_u: The HTTPS binding is not available.
sensors.transport.reason.identity_refuse: The platform refused the sensor's identity: pair or enable it again.
sensors.transport.reason.platform_certif: The gRPC endpoint's certificate does not match the platform CA the sensor pinned.
sensors.transport.reason.platform_unreac: The platform did not answer the last check; the sensor keeps its connection and checks again soon.
sensors.install.trustCollector.label: Trust this collector to push asset reports
sensors.install.trustCollector.help: A new collector starts untrusted, and the platform refuses every report it sends until it is trusted. Trusted lets it send asset reports without a job: they can add new assets but never change existing ones, and scope exclusions still apply. Tick this only for a collector you install yourself. It is audited and every administrator is notified.
sensors.install.trustCollector.noPermiss: Only an administrator who may widen sensor grants can trust a collector. You can create it now and have it trusted later on the sensor's Grant.
sensors.install.trustCollector.notApplie: The collector was created, but trusting it failed. It stays untrusted until it is promoted on the sensor's Grant.
sensors.grant.collectorRefused.untrusted: This collector's reports are refused: it is not trusted

Its grant allows asset reports, but a sensor that is not trusted cannot send results without a job, so the platform refuses every report it sends. Promote it to Trusted if you installed it and know where it runs.
sensors.grant.collectorRefused.grantTitl: This collector's reports are refused: its grant does not allow them
sensors.grant.collectorRefused.grantBody: Its grant does not allow results without a job, so the platform refuses every report it sends. Change its profile to Collector, then promote it to Trusted.
sensors.grant.collectorRefused.askAdmin: An administrator who may widen sensor grants can change this.
sensors.review.sandboxConfined: Each scan task reaches only its targets. This sensor can take jobs that need confinement (a web scope).
sensors.review.sandboxUnknown: This sensor does not report its sandbox (an older release). Jobs that need confinement go to other sensors.
sensors.review.sandboxNotConfined: Jobs that need confinement (a web scope) go to other sensors. Run the container with the sensor's seccomp profile; its setup checklist names the cause.
sensors.grant.suggestion.usage.idle: No jobs and no results without a job.
sensors.grant.suggestion.changed: The suggestion changed since it was shown. It was reloaded; review it and try again.
sensors.grant.suggestion.error: Could not apply the suggested grant
sensors.grant.suggestion.incomplete: This sensor ran too many different jobs to check them all. Pick its profile with Narrow.
sensors.grant.suggestion.noFit: No profile admits every job this sensor ran without widening its grant (for example an intrusive T2 job). Narrow it by hand with Narrow.
sensors.grant.suggestion.title: Suggested grant: {profile}
sensors.grant.suggestion.idleBody: This sensor did nothing in the window. The default profile of its kind is suggested.
sensors.grant.suggestion.body: The narrowest profile that admits every job this sensor ran. It is never wider than the current grant; the trust level is kept.
sensors.grant.suggestion.confirmDesc: From its next request the sensor gets only the jobs this profile admits. A job outside it (for example a schedule that did not run in the window) is refused and named in the sensor timeline. You may be asked to confirm your identity. This is audited.
sensors.toolSettings.title: Tool settings
sensors.toolSettings.intro: Overrides for this sensor. An option you leave empty inherits the organization's tool default, or the tool's own default. The values reach the sensor inside each signed scan job.
sensors.toolSettings.empty: No tool on this sensor declares settings yet.
sensors.toolSettings.loadError: Could not load the tool settings
sensors.toolSettings.noFields: This tool declares no settings that can be changed here.
sensors.toolSettings.staleWarning: The sensor's tool changed and these saved settings no longer fit it. Its scan jobs fail until you save or reset them.
sensors.toolSettings.t2Locked: A dangerous option keeps its default until the organization can enable dangerous options.
sensors.toolSettings.effectiveError: Could not load the effective values
sensors.manifest.loadError: The manifest could not be loaded.
sensors.manifest.empty: No manifest yet. A sensor registers one when it connects, and the platform derives one from the first heartbeat that reports its tools.
sensors.manifest.slotsDynamic: slots sized from CPU and memory
sensors.manifest.ignored.unknown-member: not part of the manifest format
sensors.toolSettings.impactWarning: A non-default value increases the load or reach of each scan.
sensors.pair.profileDesc.scan-connector: Runs one connector to a scanner product your organization runs (the Tenable.sc connector): its syncs and its scans; no scanner of its own.
sensors.checks.sdk.advisory: {sdk} has a published security advisory. Upgrade the sensor to a build with a fixed SDK.
sensors.version.sdkAdvisoryHint: This SDK release has a published security advisory
sensors.snippets.customNote: A custom sensor is your own build on the sensor SDK. Install it the way its author documents, with this sensor's API key and the platform URL. The platform checks it by protocol and capabilities, not by release.
sensors.toolSettings.orgProblems: The organization's defaults do not fit this sensor's tool version. Its scan jobs of this tool fail until the defaults change.
sensors.toolSettings.impactStepUp: Changing it asks you to confirm your identity.
sensors.toolDefaults.title: Tool defaults
sensors.toolDefaults.description: The options every sensor of your organization runs each tool with. A sensor can override any option in its own Tool settings.
sensors.toolDefaults.layersNote: Order: tool default, then these organization defaults, then a sensor's overrides. A scan or workflow step can only lower rate, concurrency and retries, and each sensor's local policy can always narrow further. Shared platform sensors never use these defaults.
sensors.toolDefaults.readOnly: Owners and administrators change these defaults.
sensors.toolDefaults.loadError: Could not load the tool defaults
sensors.toolDefaults.empty: None of your sensors reports a tool that declares settings. Tools appear here once a sensor connects and reports them.
sensors.toolDefaults.problemsTitle: These sensors' tool versions refuse the defaults, so their scan jobs of this tool fail:
sensors.toolDefaults.noSchema: No sensor reports this tool any more. Reset its defaults to remove them.
sensors.empty.title: Run your first sensor
sensors.empty.what: A sensor is a small service you run inside your network. It stays connected, takes scan jobs from the platform and reaches what the platform cannot: internal hosts, private networks and cloud accounts. Results come back over HTTPS.
sensors.empty.role.scanner.title: Scanner
sensors.empty.role.scanner.text: Discovers and scans the targets in its zone: ports, web services and vulnerabilities.
sensors.empty.role.collector.title: Collector
sensors.empty.role.collector.text: Imports assets and findings from the tools you already run.
sensors.empty.pairHint: No secret to copy: the sensor prints a code you confirm here.
sensors.empty.askAdmin: An organization admin can add a sensor.
sensors.empty.ciNoSensor: Scanning repositories from CI needs no sensor.
sensors.sharedOptOut.label: Never use shared sensors
sensors.sharedOptOut.description: Off (default): scans may run on the instance's shared sensors when it offers them. On: this organization's scans run only on its own sensors.
sensors.sharedOptOut.ownerOnly: Only the organization owner can change this.
sensors.sharedOptOut.optedOutToast: This organization no longer uses shared sensors
sensors.sharedOptOut.optedInToast: Shared sensors may be used when available
sensors.sharedOptOut.error: Could not save the shared sensor choice
sensors.shared.title: Shared sensors
sensors.shared.subtitle: Sensors this instance runs for every organization, for public targets.
sensors.shared.publicOnly: Public targets only. Internal addresses, asset groups and targets in a scan zone run on your organization's sensors.
sensors.shared.proofNeeded: Every target needs a verified domain of your organization.
sensors.shared.queueLimit: A job that waits {minutes} minutes for a free slot fails.
sensors.shared.chooseWhere: Choose where a scan runs in its Sensor setting (Auto, Organization sensors or Shared sensors).
sensors.shared.optOutHint: Your organization's scans must never run on shared sensors?
sensors.shared.optOutLink: Opt out in the organization settings
sensors.shared.egress.title: Egress addresses
sensors.shared.egress.hint: Shared sensors send traffic from these addresses. Allowlist them in your firewall or intrusion detection so scans are not blocked.
sensors.checks.sdk.unsupported: {sdk} is older than the oldest SDK this platform supports. Rebuild the sensor with a newer sdk-go.
sensors.version.sdkUnsupportedHint: This SDK release is older than the oldest this platform supports
sensors.customProducts.title: Sensor products
sensors.customProducts.description: The latest and minimum release of the sensors your organization builds itself.
sensors.customProducts.note: For sensors your organization builds on sdk-go: record the latest and the minimum release of each product to see "update available" and "unsupported" on its sensors. Without it, only SDK compatibility is shown. First-party products are managed by the platform.
sensors.customProducts.readOnly: You can view these products. Changing them needs the sensors write permission.
sensors.customProducts.suggest: Reported by your sensors, not recorded yet:
sensors.customProducts.dialogDescription: The product name is what the sensor reports. Versions look like v1.4.0.
sensors.customProducts.emptyNote: Leave a version empty to not set it.
sensors.customProducts.deleteDescription: {product} loses its recorded releases. Its sensors stop showing "update available" and "unsupported".
sensors.customProducts.empty: Add a product to track the releases of a sensor your organization builds.
sensors.jobSafety.saveFailed: Could not save the sensor job settings
sensors.jobSafety.desc: What scan jobs may do on your sensors. A sensor's own local policy always decides first; these settings only narrow what is sent.
sensors.jobSafety.jobsDesc: Sent with every scan job. Saved together with Save changes.
sensors.jobSafety.privateTargets: Private targets need a sensor-local policy
sensors.jobSafety.privateTargetsHint: Jobs that scan private addresses (RFC 1918, internal domains) go only to sensors whose network owner installed a local policy. Other sensors leave them for one that has it.
sensors.jobSafety.immediateDesc: Each switch here applies as soon as you change it.
sensors.jobSafety.loosen.title: Let scan jobs do more?
sensors.jobSafety.loosen.desc: These changes widen what scan jobs may do on your sensors. They are recorded in the audit log at high severity.
sensors.jobSafety.loosen.privateTargets: Private targets may go to sensors without a local policy.
sensors.jobSafety.loosen.interactsh: Scan jobs may use out-of-band callbacks to an external server.
sensors.jobSafety.loosen.customTemplates: Scan jobs may carry custom templates.
sensors.jobSafety.loosen.insecureTls: Scan tools may accept invalid TLS certificates.
sensors.pair.getSensor.title: Don't have the sensor yet?
sensors.pair.getSensor.body: Install the sensor on the host first. It needs only the platform URL (and the platform CA fingerprint if you use a private CA). No key is copied: the sensor makes its own when it pairs.
